messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Jay Singh <j.singh@medthera.com>, Aisha Kapoor <aisha.kapoor@medthera.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-call: MedThera secure hosting requirements & next steps

Hi Jay / Aisha — thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our 45-minute call and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned.

High-level pain & goals (as we understood them)
- Primary concern: run PHI/clinical NLP workloads without sending identifiable data to multi-tenant endpoints.
- Must support customer-managed keys (CMK) for encryption at rest and in transit.
- Network constraint: strictly controlled egress; infrastructure sits behind corporate firewall with a proxy and limited outbound CIDRs.
- Regulatory: internal auditors expect immutable audit logs and 3-year retention for access records.
- Performance: batch inference for nightly ETL and sub-200ms tail latency for interactive clinician workflows.

Current stack & constraints you described
- Kubernetes on-prem (Rancher-managed) with dedicated nodes for analytics; EHR vendor (HealthCore) in the mix.
- Legacy ETL jobs that currently make outbound calls to third-party transforms.
- KMS provider: Azure Key Vault today (planning to centralize).

Success criteria for initial pilot
- Private deployment (VPC/air-gapped option) with CMK integration and no customer data leaving MedThera-managed network.
- Proof-of-concept demonstrating token-level audit logs exported to your SIEM.
- Agreed acceptance tests: sample throughput, latency, and security checklist items.

Attachments I’m sharing (preview): medthera-infra-diagram.pdf (example mapping), redwood-security-summary.pdf (controls & attestations), proposed-map.xlsx (agenda & attendee suggestions).

Proposed next steps
1) Tech deep-dive (60–90m) — target week of Oct 12; attendees: your infra + security + proxy/firewall lead, our runtime/ops + security engineer (Vanessa). Please confirm preferred slots.
2) Share a non-sensitive network diagram (CIDRs, proxy egress, NAT gateways) ahead of the call — Jay, you mentioned a sketch you could share.
3) Security questionnaire & sample CMK flow: Redwood to send a pre-read (we attached a one-pager).
4) Legal/procurement: Marissa will prepare an initial NDA/term-sheet stub to speed procurement.

If any of the above is off-base, flag it and I’ll update. Happy to schedule the deep-dive — Vanessa will propose times.

Thanks,
Sean
Sean Gallagher

Thanks Sean — useful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 
- We do have a legacy ETL pipeline that requires selective outbound connections to a transform vendor (vendor endpoints are allowed by IP). We will need to preserve that for the pilot — can Redwood support explicit egress allow-lists?
- Audit requirement: our compliance team needs immutable access logs retained for 36 months and tamper-evidence for any deletion attempts.
- KMS: we plan to centralize on Azure Key Vault but can explore HSM-backed keys for the pilot if Redwood supports an HSM/KMS proxy.

I can share a quick network sketch (attached) and our infra lead can join the technical call. Tuesday Oct 13 (morning PT) works for us for the deep-dive — can Vanessa propose a specific time?

Hi Jay / team — looping in a proposed agenda and artifact checklist for the technical deep-dive. Thanks again for sharing the sketch.

Proposed agenda (60–90 minutes)
- Introductions & scope alignment (5–10m)
- Network architecture & egress constraints (20–25m) — MedThera to present CIDRs, proxy/NAT behavior, and any SSL-intercepting appliances.
- KMS/CMK integration options (15–20m) — how Redwood integrates with Azure Key Vault or on-prem HSMs, key rotation model.
- Deployment model options (20m) — VPC vs air-gapped node groups, isolation patterns, and caching/KV strategies.
- Acceptance criteria & integration checklist (10m)

Pre-read / artifacts requested
- Network diagram with CIDRs and proxy egress points (we received your sketch — thanks).
- Example firewall rules for outbound (allow-list IPs, ports 443, etc.).
- KMS provider details (Azure Key Vault endpoint, any HSM requirements).
- A contact for your security/proxy team to validate SSL/TLS interception behavior.

I attached Redwood's security controls summary for quick review. I’ll create a calendar invite for Tue Oct 13 10:00 AM PT / 1:00 PM ET — please confirm if that slot works, or suggest alternatives.

Hi Aisha / Jay — I’m the Redwood lead on legal/procurement. Short note on next steps from a contracting perspective: 

- NDA: I’ve prepared a two-way mutual NDA (link to DocuSign included in related links). If you prefer your template, we can review and mark edits in redline, but using our standard NDA will speed up the POC kickoff.
- Commercial timeline: for a pilot with a Reserved/Private deployment we typically need 4–6 weeks from signed NDA to environment readiness (depends on your ops bandwidth and any air-gap work).
- Security/compliance artifacts: if you can sign the NDA we’ll provide SOC-type evidence and a checklist of required attestations.

I’ll wait to see the technical deep-dive outcomes before drafting a pilot SOW and initial term-sheet. In parallel I can start a draft statement-of-work keyed to the acceptance criteria Sean outlined.
